title: Round at a Complete Literal
statement: Let $x,p,r$ be bit strings, $j$ a natural number, $q$ a streaming phase other than $0$ or $4$, and $\ell$ a literal over natural-number variables. Suppose $x$ is the concatenation of $p$, the binary encoding of $\ell$, and $r$. If $q=3$ and $r$ begins with $1$, the round emits the encoding of $(j,1)$, then $0,1$, then the encoding of $(j,0)$, followed by the encoding of $\ell$; it advances the cursor to $j+1$ and the consumed length by the encoded length of $\ell$, leaving the phase at $3$. Otherwise it emits just the encoding of $\ell$, leaves the cursor at $j$, advances the consumed length by that encoded length, and sets the phase to $2$ when $q=1$ and to $3$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $q$ is a phase in the five-element phase set
$\ell$ is a literal over natural-number variables
$x=p$ followed by the encoding of $\ell$ and then $r$
replaced:
Let the input be $p$ followed by a serialized literal $\ell$ and a remainder $r$,
and let the seam state have consumed $|p|$ bits in a literal phase (neither
formula nor finished). If the phase is the tail phase and $r$ starts with a clause
bit $1$, the round allocates the fresh cursor $j$: it emits the positive link
$(j,\mathrm{true})$, two markers, the negative literal $(j,\mathrm{false})$, and
$\ell$, incrementing the cursor; otherwise it emits $\ell$ verbatim and advances
the phase. In both cases the consumed length advances by the serialized literal
length, so no literal buffer survives a round boundary.
